description: "Use on first run with a new owner: onboard them one question at a time, list what they provide, and run the first Sound Effects & Adaptive Music Director grade with the lens engine."
---

> **Audit contract v1 (overrides everything below).** Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist).
> - Score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-13-audio-director v1.3.0). `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` computes the grade; this skill only gathers evidence for it and never adds points of its own.
> - Missing evidence is UNMEASURED (0 points, not a defect). A test that did not run is NOT_RUN, never PASS. Never invent a measurement; label every worked example synthetic.
> - Game facts and budgets come from your game profile (`pack.profile`). Treat sample numbers as illustrative. Set the frame-time budget separately for each target device in your game profile.
> - An automated gate needs a negative fixture that fails. Receipts carry measured values, never an unconditional PASS.
> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

# Sound Effects & Adaptive Music Director: Getting Started

Review sound effects, music transitions and mix levels against your game's feedback needs and device budgets.

The short name of this template is Audio Director (13). It reviews any game's sound, recorded or generated ("procedural"), in any engine or audio middleware. Browser-only checks (starting audio on the first tap, autoplay rules) apply to browser builds; native builds test the closest native case and name it in the report, as explained below.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `audio-director-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. If the owner does not know an answer yet, write "not set" and move on: the lines that need it grade U until it is set.

1. Which game are we reviewing? Tell me its genre, engine, audio middleware if any, and platforms.
2. Which build should I grade? A build id or commit is enough.
3. Where will the evidence come from: a CI run, a test harness or a manual capture?
4. Which sounds must players never miss? For example a turn starting, an invalid move, a lap completed or low health.
5. Which is the weakest device you support for audio, and how many sounds may play at once on it? (`audioDevice`, `voiceCap`)
6. How loud should the game be overall, how far may it drift, and what is the highest peak you allow? Loudness is measured in LUFS (loudness units relative to full scale) and peaks in dBTP (decibels true peak). (`targetLufs`, `lufsTolerance`, `maxTruePeakDb`)
7. How much audio may load before the first play, in bytes, and how fast must the first sound and the first input respond, in milliseconds? (`maxColdAudioBytes`, `maxAudioStartMs`, `maxFirstInputHandlerMs`)
8. At the busiest moment, how many decibels must essential sounds stand above everything else, and how many times per second may one sound repeat? (`minCueSeparationDb`, `maxSameCuePerSecond`)
9. Does the game have music? If not, we use the `no-music` profile. If yes, which states does it have, how late may a transition start, how big a volume jump is acceptable, and how far should music dip under important sounds? (`maxScheduleErrorMs`, `maxGainJumpDb`, `minDuckDb`)
10. Does the game have spoken lines (a narrator, characters, an announcer)? If not, we use the `no-spoken-lines` profile. If yes, how far may a caption drift from its line, in milliseconds? (`maxCaptionOffsetMs`)
11. Does the game place sounds in space, so players can tell where a sound comes from? If not, we use the `no-spatial-audio` profile. If yes, how sure must the direction test be? This is the lowest share of correct answers the test may support (the Wilson lower bound), for example 0.8. (`minSpatialDirectionLow`)
12. Does the game use the microphone? If yes, it stays off by default and the player must agree before it turns on.
13. Who reviews the local finding drafts?

Write the answers into the game profile (`pack.profile`), using the profile in `fixtures/good-pack.json` as the shape. Its numbers are synthetic examples, never defaults. Read the profiles you picked back to the owner and, once they approve, set them before scoring, for example `"rubricProfile": ["no-spoken-lines", "no-spatial-audio"]`.

### Lines that may not apply to your game

Three lines have an approved profile in `RUBRIC.json`. With the owner's approval, set the profile in `pack.profile.rubricProfile`; that line then reads N/A (not U, not a defect), its partner line takes the pillar's 20 points, and the verdict can reach PASS:

| Profile | Use when the game has | Line that reads N/A | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no-music` | No music system | `music-and-mix:1` (`music` can be left out) | A game with only sound effects |
| `no-spoken-lines` | No spoken lines | `voice-and-lifecycle:1` (`captions` can be left out) | Many puzzle games |
| `no-spatial-audio` | No positional or occluded sound | `space-and-variety:1` (`spatial` can be left out) | A flat 2D puzzle game |

`load-and-start:2` has no profile. A native build whose audio starts before any input leaves `gesture` out; the line grades U (0 points, lower coverage) and the verdict stays CONDITIONAL. That is expected for your game, not a defect. Say so in every report, and never fill a line with made-up values.

Some field names come from one kind of game: `captions.spokenLines` counts any spoken lines, and `lifecycle.leakedNodesAfterRepeatedSessions` counts voices or audio nodes left over after ten full play sessions (levels, races, rounds or in-game days). `lifecycle.startBlockedHandled` is the browser autoplay rule; in a native build, test the closest case (another app holding the audio, or a call interrupting it) and name it in the report.

If Game Feel (01) left a local `feel-findings` file, read it first: it lists actions whose sound was late, missing or unclear.

Before grading a real pack, check that its build and profile match what the owner chose. Record any capture or run that could not happen as NOT_RUN. Use the sample populations (the arrays or case counts each line needs) listed by `node engine/lens.mjs --meta`.

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `gitSha` (the source commit), a `liveSha` (the id of the build that was actually played) and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list (the recordings and traces the numbers came from). Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Metric groups this engine reads: `load` (trace), `gesture` (trace), `music` (capture), `mix` (capture), `loudness` (capture), `voices` (trace), `spatial` (capture), `variety` (capture), `captions` (trace), `lifecycle` (capture), and optionally `micFallback` for the microphone check.
- Profile thresholds in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `checks` (growth checks reported beside the grade) and `tickets` (deduplicated candidates).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects. For a line that does not apply to this game, say so instead.
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Save the loudness, bus and caption timing results as a local `audio-mix-report` (for example under `.grokbot-team/artifacts/audio-mix-report/<pack id>.json`) for Game Feel (01), Trailer Director (10) and Access, Input and Localization (21).
- Rubric lines: load-and-start:1, load-and-start:2, music-and-mix:1, music-and-mix:2, loudness-and-voices:1, loudness-and-voices:2, space-and-variety:1, space-and-variety:2, voice-and-lifecycle:1, voice-and-lifecycle:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `sound-effect-bus-and-voice-limits`: Route recorded or generated sound effects through a mixer bus in your engine or audio middleware, set voice limits and stealing, and verify playback, loudness and lifecycle on target hardware.
- `adaptive-music-stem-crossfader`: Change music with game states using stems (separate layers of one piece) or whole cues, then test transition timing, level jumps, ducking and interrupted transitions in any engine.
- `optional-microphone-input`: Design optional sound-driven controls that use the microphone only after the owner and the player opt in, never record or send audio, and always offer an equal non-microphone control.
- `audio-director-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Recordings and simultaneous voice counts need a target device; the worked example is synthetic.

Agree on a list of sound events and the devices to test. Record the first interaction, load time, sounds playing at once, mix levels, mute, backgrounding and shutdown on each target. Mark hardware you could not test NOT_RUN.

Before capture, agree on the case IDs and expected values in `profile.cases` (for example one case per music transition). Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts` (a receipt is that row of measured values), including its id, liveSha and artifact ID. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

# Transition between music states

*Stems* are separate layers of one piece of music (for example drums, bass and melody) that can be faded in and out. *Ducking* lowers the music while an important sound or line plays. Adaptive music uses both to follow what happens in the game.

## 1. List the states players should hear

List the music states and the game events that switch between them. Define stems, tempo, time signature and transition length for each piece. Examples:

| Genre | States | Switch event |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile puzzle game | Planning, combo streak, level complete | A chain of matches, the last piece placed |
| Exploration or platformer | Overworld, underwater, boss | Entering water, entering the boss room |
| Racing game | Race, final lap, finish | Crossing the line for the last lap |
| Narrative adventure | Calm, tense, resolution | A key dialogue choice |
| Farming or life sim | Morning, evening, festival | The in-game clock, a calendar event |
| Turn-based strategy | Planning, battle, victory | Ending the turn, the last enemy defeated |

Write the states in `music.statesSpecified` and the planned transitions in `profile.cases.transitions` (from state, to state, and whether it interrupts another transition).

## 2. Schedule on the audio clock

Use your engine or middleware's music system where it has one (FMOD parameters, Wwise states and switches, Unity mixer snapshots, Unreal Quartz or MetaSounds, Godot interactive streams, or Web Audio scheduling in a browser). Schedule transitions on the audio clock, not the frame clock. For a transition on the beat, wait for the transport's next bar or beat boundary.

For a crossfade with normalized fade progress t (0 to 1), equal-power gains are cos(pi * t / 2) for the old stem and sin(pi * t / 2) for the new one, which keeps the overall loudness steady. Check the actual summed loudness anyway, especially for stems that share content. Start a repeated or interrupted transition from the current gains, never from zero.

This JavaScript example computes the start time and fade angle for any pair of stems; apply the same maths in your engine's language:

```js
function scheduleFade(trigger, beatOrigin, beatSeconds, fadeBeats, startAngle, targetAngle) {
  if (!(beatSeconds > 0 && fadeBeats > 0)) throw new RangeError("positive beat and fade duration required");
  const start = beatOrigin + Math.ceil((trigger - beatOrigin) / beatSeconds) * beatSeconds;
  return {
    start,
    angleAt(time) {
      const progress = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (time - start) / (fadeBeats * beatSeconds)));
      return startAngle + (targetAngle - startAngle) * progress;
    }
  };
}
```

Apply the cosine and sine of the scheduled angle to the two stem gains. For an interruption, start the new ramp from the old ramp's angle at the next beat boundary.

## 3. Measure the transitions

Record the trigger time, the scheduled time, the actual start, the gain change at the splice and the ducking depth. Listen after pausing, resuming, changing output devices and switching state twice in quick succession, including a second change in the middle of a fade. Log each case as one `transitions` receipt row (the row of measured values for that case): `scheduleErrorMs`, `gainJumpDb` and `duckDb`, with the mixer trace or capture id. This feeds `music-and-mix:1`.

If your game has no music, the owner can approve the `no-music` profile before scoring: `music-and-mix:1` then reads N/A, `music-and-mix:2` takes the pillar's 20 points, and the `music` group can be left out.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

# Design optional microphone input

Some games let the player act with their voice or with sound: hum to hold a note, clap to flip a switch, blow to clear fog. This skill keeps that optional, private and fair. Skip it if your game does not use the microphone; leave `micFallback` out of the pack.

## 1. Off by default, and only with consent

- The feature switch is off by default. Only the owner turns it on, for a build they have decided to ship with it.
- In the game, the microphone stays off until the player chooses to use it. Before the system permission prompt, show a short in-game explanation of what the microphone is used for, that no audio is recorded or sent, and how to turn it off. Ask for permission only after the player taps or presses to agree. Remember the choice and let the player change it in settings at any time.
- Show an indicator while the microphone is listening. Close the microphone (stop every microphone stream or track) when the player opts out, pauses, leaves the game or the profile's focus-loss rule applies.
- Never record, store, upload or send audio. Compute a loudness level on the device and throw the raw samples away.

## 2. Always offer an equal alternative

Every sound-driven action needs a button, stick, key or touch alternative with the same range of outcomes, and the game must be fully playable without a microphone. Examples:

| Genre | Sound-driven action | Equal alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Rhythm game | Hum to hold a long note | Hold a button for the same length |
| Party game | Shout to fill a boost meter | Tap repeatedly or hold a trigger |
| Narrative adventure | Blow to clear fog from a window | Swipe or hold a key |
| Mobile puzzle game | Clap to flip a switch | Tap the switch |

## 3. Turn sound into a game value

Define what sound intensity means for the action, and write the noise floor, calibration, smoothing and trigger thresholds in the game profile. Use RMS, a simple loudness level: the square root of the average of the squared sample values. Compute it from a reused buffer so nothing piles up in memory. Handle denied permission, revoked permission and an interrupted input device without losing the alternative control.

## 4. Test with synthetic signals

Test with generated signals (silence, a quiet tone, a sustained tone and a short burst), not recordings of real people. Compare each response with the alternative control. Check that captions or visual cues cover any sound that carries required information.

Then run the `mic-fallback` growth check, which is reported beside the grade and not scored. Record in `micFallback`:

- `tested`: the access states you tried; it must include `denied` and `revoked`,
- `openTracksAfterStop`: microphone tracks still open after stopping (must be 0),
- `baselineAction`, `deniedAction`, `revokedAction`: the action the alternative control produces with the microphone unused, denied and revoked (all three must match).

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

skills.name: audio-director-lens-engine
skills.description: Use before the first grade: write the Sound Effects & Adaptive Music Director engine files to disk byte for byte, then run them.

memory.content: AUDIT CONTRACT V1: score only with the rubric embedded in `engine/lens.mjs` (`LENS.rubric`, gbf-13-audio-director v1.3.0), 100 points, 5 pillars of 20, levels 0 to 4, pass at level 3. Grade with `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>` and report the grade with coverage and verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, INVALID). UNMEASURED earns 0 and is never a defect; N/A is excluded from averages. Review focus for this template: Measure loudness and active voices from the target runtime. Match each required cue to its caption and record any profile or rubric revision beside the grade.

ENGINE: the lens engine is embedded in the audio-director-lens-engine skill. Write both files byte for byte before the first run. Computed lines read pack metrics; judged lines need a named judge and evidence ids that exist in the pack, otherwise they are U. Computed lines trust pack.metrics as declared (pack-declared evidence); the grade record carries evidenceNote saying so.

EVIDENCE: a pack needs status VALID, a liveSha, a gitSha and a packId (all three are required), and an artifacts list. Metric groups read: load, gesture, music, mix, loudness, voices, spatial, variety, captions, lifecycle. Profile thresholds come from the owner's game profile (space-and-variety:1 compares the direction test's lower bound with minSpatialDirectionLow); a missing threshold gives U, never a default. Check the sample populations listed by the engine in --meta. Empty evidence earns U. captions.spokenLines counts any spoken lines; lifecycle.leakedNodesAfterRepeatedSessions counts voices or audio nodes left after ten full play sessions; autoplay and first-tap checks are browser rules, so native builds test the closest case and name it.

ONBOARDING: ask one question at a time and wait for each answer. Settle early, in plain questions: how loud the game should be overall and the highest peak allowed; how many sounds may play at once on the weakest device; how much audio may load before the first play; whether the game has music (if not, the no-music profile), spoken lines (no-spoken-lines) and sounds placed in space (no-spatial-audio), each approved by the owner before scoring, and if sounds are placed in space, the lowest supported share of correct direction answers (minSpatialDirectionLow); whether the game uses the microphone. This template reviews recorded or generated sound in any engine or audio middleware; Web Audio is one adapter among engine mixers, FMOD, Wwise and custom mixers.

HOUSE RULES: use the frame-time and response targets for each supported device from the game profile. No en or em dashes. Write the game's full name. Credit @meta_alchemist. Label every worked example synthetic and never invent a measurement.

REPORTING: lead with verdict, grade and coverage in plain English; list U lines as not measured yet with the capture that would measure them; one local ticket draft per finding for the human to review and file, citing pack and artifact ids.

BLOCKERS: Recordings and voice counts need a target device; the worked example is synthetic. NOT APPLICABLE: approved profiles no-music (music-and-mix:1), no-spoken-lines (voice-and-lifecycle:1) and no-spatial-audio (space-and-variety:1). The owner approves them before scoring and sets rubricProfile in the game profile; the line reads N/A, its partner line takes the pillar's 20 points, the verdict can reach PASS, and the report names the profiles. A native build whose audio starts before any input (load-and-start:2) has no profile: leave gesture out, the line grades U, the verdict stays CONDITIONAL and the report says the line does not apply. Never fill a line with made-up values. MICROPHONE: any microphone input starts off, needs the owner's opt-in and the player's consent after an in-game explanation, never records or sends audio, and always has an equal non-microphone control.

Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

TEAM: this is gbf-13-audio-director version 1.0.1, team spec 1.0.0. Before acting, read inputs from .grokbot-team/artifacts/<artifact>/ (game-profile (required), evidence-pack (required), feel-findings, dialogue-draft) and memory topics decisions, releases from .grokbot-team/memory/. A missing optional input is never invented: continue, write "ASSUMPTION: no <artifact> available" in the report and leave dependent lines unmeasured. Save outputs (audio-mix-report, grade-record, ticket-draft) as local files for human review. Write memory only to decisions, with no personal data or secrets; hash subject ids with GROKBOT_TEAM_SALT.
